full_details: You sat over the king from the first gage through to the castle wall. The joins are still marks: here a messenger, here York, angry. One passage had been carrying the wrong weight because it was pleasant to write, and you drew a line down its margin and did not copy the speech out. You named what is unfinished. The deposing, the prison, the end. You did not write them. At the Jackdaw, Ralph Raye brought the Rose with the dinner. Henslowe has paid his carpenters seven pounds and two shillings for a throne in the heavens, a chair that comes down out of the roof. Yesterday's new play on the Bankside was The Seven Days of the Week, at three pounds ten. James Burbage showed the rigging with a knife and a crust, and said he could build a heavens for five pound if he had five pound and a lease. Pope proposed they lower Kemp. Kemp asked to be winched down on a barrel. You said a glass, four shillings, comes down by itself, and that a boy and two men with clean verse can build a castle out of air, and it costs nothing to strike.
one_sentence: You read the king from the first gage to the castle wall, and at dinner heard of a throne in the heavens.
title: A line in the margin, and a throne in the heavens
